Here’s a mix of classic, contemporary, and cult‑favorite horror films that span various sub‑genres. Pick whatever mood strikes you!

| # | Title | Year | Sub‑genre | Why it’s worth watching |
|---|-------|------|-----------|------------------------|
| 1 | **Psycho** | 1960 | Psychological Thriller | Hitchcock’s masterclass in suspense; the shower scene is legendary. |
| 2 | **The Shining** | 1980 | Supernatural / Psychological Horror | Kubrick’s eerie adaptation of Stephen King’s novel; haunting visuals & performances. |
| 3 | **Halloween** | 1978 | Slasher | John Carpenter’s iconic killer, Michael Myers; the film set the template for the genre. |
| 4 | **The Exorcist** | 1973 | Paranormal / Religious Horror | One of the most chilling exorcism stories ever told; still unnerving today. |
| 5 | **Hereditary** | 2018 | Psychological / Family Horror | A deeply unsettling family drama that escalates into pure terror. |
| 6 | **Get Out** | 2017 | Social Commentary / Horror | Jordan Peele blends satire with genuine scares; a fresh take on racial tension. |
| 7 | **A Quiet Place** | 2018 | Survival / Sci‑Fi Horror | Silence is survival; the film’s sound design is as terrifying as its monsters. |
| 8 | **It Follows** | 2014 | Modern Urban Legend | A unique premise where a curse follows you; the film’s atmosphere is relentless. |
| 9 | **Midsommar** | 2019 | Folk Horror | Daylight horror at its best; the film’s rituals are both beautiful and grotesque. |
|10 | **The Ring** | 2002 | Japanese Horror Adaptation | A cursed videotape that turns into a modern urban legend; the film’s pacing is tight. |

Feel free to let me know if you’d like recommendations tailored to a specific era, sub‑genre, or even a particular director!
